answer: Agents deter Sybil attacks via modulated optical retroreflection. A verifier projects a laser beacon across an elevated ridge toward candidate nodes. Each agent authenticates by modulating the beam with a steerable mirror to return signed challenge data. Adversaries cannot virtualize nodes because valid responses demand dedicated optical hardware and physical line-of-sight per identity. However, thermal turbulence refracts the beam, causing intermittent verification dropouts.
